rewrite.description: Exactly one item, kind=outline, holding the ordered `lines` -- Claude never produces any other kind for a new analysis. Older kinds (summary/definition/bullets/steps/table/callout/paragraph) stay valid to DECODE an analysis saved by an earlier version, but are never requested from Claude again.

lines.description: The whole rewrite, paragraph by paragraph, as a single ordered sequence of typed lines.

type.description: point: one main bullet per source paragraph. subpoint: a supporting detail nested under the last point/consequence. explanation: one short line of plain-prose explanation nested under the last point/consequence (Word style 'Spiegazione bullet'), not a sub-bullet -- at most one per point. note: a standalone aside worth setting apart (Word style 'Nota'). formula: a short formula, equation or fixed expression worth setting apart in its own line (Word style 'Formula'). consequence: a point that states a cause's effect/result (replaces the old '-> ' prefix convention; same level as point). subheading: a rare divider title INSIDE a section that has real unmarked sub-parts (Word style 'Grasso Titoli') -- it is never a title of the document's own index/table of contents (T1-T4), just a quiet divider line. definition: a standalone line (same level as point) used ONLY when the block's own text explicitly defines a term or concept; it states the term and its meaning as the text gives them (Word style 'Definizione'). example: a standalone line (same level as point) used ONLY for a concrete example, case or illustration that the block's own text actually presents as one (Word style 'Example').
